customer_feedback_verbatim: Customer wanted to know whether his car includes the remote control parking feature and, if it does, how to operate it. Writer verified that the vehicle is indeed equipped with remote control parking. Writer then called the customer back and walked him through the steps for using it. Writer first confirmed the customer already has the digital key plus configured on his device, and customer answered yes. Writer advised that he should begin the automatic parking process as he normally does by pressing the P button at low speed to bring up the parking cameras, which customer acknowledged. Writer then explained that once parking is activated, he must press the brake, set the parking brake, and follow the on-screen prompt to continue with the maneuver assistant. Writer instructed that after choosing that option, he should exit the car and open the My BMW App, select the remote control parking tile on the main screen, and then follow the instructions to move the phone forward and backward to align with the two targets. Writer added that once that is done, he needs to press and hold the blue circle in the app to finish the parking process. Customer stated he understood and said he would test it out.

customer_feedback_verbatim: Customer reported the vehicle has inconsistent scheduled charging, with the car often ignoring the programmed 8:30 PM time slot. Customer noted that sometimes it begins charging immediately after being plugged in even though the settings are not set to charge right away, and at other times it will unexpectedly start charging around 5 PM or 4 PM despite being set for 8:30 PM. Customer stated the system will also change the charging configuration on its own, switching from the time slot setting to charge immediately without any action from the customer. Customer estimated this behavior occurs about half the time, with the other 50 percent working as intended. Customer indicated the issue happens whether charging from roughly 75 percent state of charge to a 90 percent target or at other battery levels, and that it was present both before and after a software update. Customer stated all charging is done at home using a 250 volt outlet in the garage. Customer mentioned the AC limit was originally at 48 amps but later reduced to 32 amps to be cautious, and the problem occurs at both limits. Customer added the outlet is capable of supporting up to 48 amps. Customer advised the vehicle was brought to the dealership, but technicians were unable to duplicate the problem even though the customer provided app screenshots showing the time slot at 8:30 PM while the car charged at 8 PM. Customer said the dealership performed tests and reached out to BMW engineers, but they were unable to resolve the issue. Customer stated the dealership did not reset the software or apply any fix, and engineers concluded there was nothing to be done. Writer suggested the customer continue to observe the charging behavior and contact the dealership again if the problem persists so they can try to reproduce and diagnose it.

customer_feedback_verbatim:
Customer stated he is worried about how the range is estimated. Customer stated he drove a 100 mile round trip into the city and back home. Customer stated the car showed roughly 200 miles of range at departure and less than 60 miles remaining once he got back. Customer stated he used efficient mode only for part of the drive home because he began to doubt if there was enough charge to reach his house. Customer stated the average outside temperature was about 32-35 degrees. Customer stated he did not precondition the vehicle before leaving, but the car was kept in his garage overnight. Customer stated the dealership did not clearly explain how to get the best range, and that this is his first electric vehicle.

Writer advised the figure in the instrument cluster is only an estimate. Writer advised that range is affected by climate control usage, driving style, charging behavior, weather, road terrain, and some other variables. Writer advised that preconditioning the vehicle on a cold day will provide a much more accurate range prediction. Writer advised that heating the vehicle up to optimal temperature consumes a lot of battery power, and that not just the cabin but also the battery itself must be warmed to operate efficiently.

i'm pleased overall but not as thrilled as i thought i would be. a few small tweaks would really help.

on the positive side, the audio system and in-car phone are excellent. i especially value the speakerphone performance.

for an ev it truly still handles like a bmw, and i'm glad for that.

customer_feedback_verbatim:
1. forward collision warning and automatic emergency braking
this car is supposed to come with standard forward collision warning and automatic emergency braking, but those features basically do not work. i have contacted your technical support several times, and although they made some tweaks, the system still does not function.

in june 2025 i brought the car in again for checks. the technical advisor, michael, rode with me and we tried different driving situations and maneuvers, yet the system never reacted at all, no warning lights, no alerts, no braking. i also tried it myself on i-25 at highway speeds, deliberately getting within about 5 feet of other vehicles, and it still failed to activate.

the sensor area has been kept clean and clear, we have gone through all the settings and looked at the owner's manual, but the problem continues.

i realize the collision avoidance is only meant to assist, not replace careful driving, but i got used to relying heavily on a similar setup in my previous lexus. i expected the bmw system to work at least as well and would like ongoing help to find a fix.

2. homelink garage door opener
the second issue is with homelink. two of your technical advisors came to my home to try and pair it with my garage opener, but they couldn't get it to sync. later i brought in a professional opener technician from liftpro, who finally managed to create a connection, yet the homelink is still unreliable and only works now and then.

most of the time when i come home, the car will not open the garage door. i end up parking, going in through the front door, and opening the garage by hand, which basically defeats having the integrated system in the first place.

customer_feedback_verbatim: Customer stated he has been experiencing connection problems with his iPhone 14 Pro Max on AT&T staying linked to the vehicle when using Apple CarPlay. Customer stated he plans to have his service department investigate the connection issues while the car is in for a recall. Writer advised that there are specific steps to follow that can help improve the connections. Writer advised: 1) Update the phone to the latest iOS, as phone software (iOS 16.6, 16.6.1) has been causing connection problems in the vehicle. 2) Remove the phone from the vehicle's Mobile Devices menu/app. 3) Remove the vehicle from the phone's Bluetooth menu. 4) Go into the CarPlay section in the phone's general settings and tap Forget This Car. 5) Perform a hard reset (force restart) of the iPhone by: a. pressing and quickly releasing the volume up button, b. pressing and quickly releasing the volume down button, c. pressing and holding the side button, d. releasing the side button when the Apple logo appears. 6) Restart the BMW headunit with a telecommunications reboot: a. make sure the engine or motor is turned on, b. press and hold the volume button for 70 seconds, during which the iDrive screen will turn off and on, and c. once the screen turns off the third time, release the volume button. 7) Confirm that phone Wi-Fi is turned on but not connected to another source. 8) Add the device again in the iDrive Mobile Devices menu/app and follow the prompts between the vehicle and phone. 9) Connect to Apple CarPlay when asked. Writer also emailed these instructions to the customer.

customer_feedback_verbatim: i really love the i5 edrive 40 and have been a dedicated 5-series fan for more than 20 years. recommending it to friends or family is another matter though, since they may not share my tastes or enthusiasm. as good as the i5 is, i feel it would be better with lithium iron phosphate batteries so we wouldn't have to worry about charging all the way to 100% regularly. being advised to stop at 80% seems restrictive, because we paid for the extra range but can't consistently use it. in my case the battery drops from 80 to about 20 every roughly 4 - 5 days, which is fine for me. however, those used to filling gasoline cars every couple of weeks might be put off by needing to recharge two or three times as often as they refuel now.

customer_feedback_verbatim: the apps built into the car really ought to be reachable from the phone, so you don't have to sit in the car and fiddle with them - you can do that in a mercedes, which was my previous car. the windows also can't be closed via the app, while mercedes manages that. if they could close themselves automatically when it rains, like mercedes does, i haven't found any sign that they do, but they should. the car has locked me out several times when i've left either the phone or the keys inside. settings in the app like folding the mirrors when locking don't actually work when it's other users, even though the option is set in the app. my wife is forced to type in a pin code and can't just pick her id, supposedly because of the risk that her phone might be stolen - but the primary user's phone can be stolen too, so that explanation doesn't make sense. the information shown in the dashboard is poor no matter which view you choose. the radio will not receive a signal while i'm driving through the limfjord tunnel, which i go through every day, and that's something i've never run into with any other car i've owned. the winter range is deeply reprehensible and honestly my biggest complaint: no more winter holiday trips, because the real range on the motorway at 130 kmh in frost is at most about 250 km. well, i guess i have to stop somewhere, but i'm left disappointed. mvh mads

customer_feedback_verbatim:
great:
* very comfortable and quiet.
* excellent handling, with precise steering.
* interior is practical and modern; quality has been great so far.
* seats are comfy, veganza material feels nice.
* good balance between real buttons and software controls.
* efficient, averaging around 3.6 mi/kwh.
* autopilot functions well.

neutral:
* does it really need to be about 200" long? i would prefer it a bit shorter.

not so great:
* adaptive suspension was not available as an option on e40.
* rear-wheel steering was also not available as an option on e40.
* sun visor is too short and will not reach the b pillar when turned to the side.
* apple carplay should come switched on by default, and bmw should allow it to occupy the entire instrument cluster.
* apple maps' design and software execution beat bmw os and will stay better for years.
* apple maps ought to show up in the head-up display; bmw maps just drawing a few lines in the hud is not helpful.
* using the right steering wheel button to control apple music only works sometimes.
* the artistic drive modes are basically a gimmick.
* not a fan of the base 2-spoke steering wheel look; the sport wheel looks better.
* autopilot complains too often when it decides you're not paying attention.

Customer stated that when he uses the blinker the way the car brakes seems logical in relation to how far away he is from the turn he is about to make, and the system then applies braking. Customer explained it took him some time to get used to this, because he feels like he should be doing the braking himself and now, when he is braking and the car is braking at the same time, it can feel a bit jolty. Customer noted that sometimes at a stop sign or street light the car clearly detects the stop sign or light, because it will show a small symbol of a stop sign or street light in the heads-up display, but he said that does not happen very frequently. Customer estimated that at a stop sign maybe around 20% of the time the system will recognize it and display it in the heads-up display, but most of the time it does not, which he finds confusing. Customer stated it is similar for street lights, and that he has only seen it show a red light symbol in the heads-up display once or twice when he comes up to a red light, while the vast majority of the time that symbol does not appear.

customer_feedback_verbatim:
overall the car is really great, and there's a lot to appreciate about it both when i'm driving and as someone who owns it. i'm obsessed with how it looks; i honestly get giddy every time i walk up to it. the build quality is the main reason i picked this instead of a model s, and as a car it's fantastic. launch mode, the light bar, all sorts of details are just awesome. but i still only give it about a 7 or 8 out of 10 because of the range, the seats, the way you can (or can't) customize things, and the cabin space.

range - i get the mindset that if it's electric then it's meant to be a commuter, but that really doesn't fit every demographic or psychographic. i work from home, so most of the time it's just driving me around town and to the airport, but the car is so addictive to drive that we're now actively planning road trips and at the same time complaining about its range. there are areas of our state, utah, that we simply can't go to because the charging infrastructure just isn't there yet.

on top of that, i'm really annoyed that you rolled out a mid-cycle efficiency update on the i5 only about four months after i bought mine.

seat comfort - i have a hard time getting comfortable in these seats. people like me with office jobs usually don't have perfect backs, so we need a way to make the seat flatter and less curved in certain spots to be comfortable. the lumbar is too aggressive by default and you can't get the seat bottom to go truly flat either. having more adjustment options would be very welcome. let the seat move to a completely neutral position first, then let us tailor things from that baseline.

cabin space - this is the most money i've ever paid for a car, and even though the i5 is about the same size as a 7-series was ten years ago, my rear passengers have less room than they did in my 2009 nissan altima. way too much space has been allocated to the trunk. even giving the back seat one extra inch of legroom would improve it. i'm 6 feet tall, and with the comfort exits turned on, when i get out or in i basically crunch whoever is sitting behind me. that's not acceptable for a car in this price range.

in-car & app customization - personal mode should really be a blend of the best parts of all the different driving modes. i want personal mode to truly mean personal. for example, i love the sounds from expression mode, but i don't want the rest of expression mode active; so why can't i pull just those sounds into personal, or bring any single setting from the other modes into personal mode? on the app side, my 2022 hyundai tucson actually offers more customization, especially around the climate controls. i get that you're aiming for a simple "one button, no thinking" climate concept, but i want the ability to build my own climate profiles: like a winter@80deg setting with seat heaters, or a summer@65 setting with the seat coolers on. the last-used climate setup isn't always what i want the car to return to when i get back in. tesla is really doing great things in their app right now; pretty much any function on the car has an api call and can be accessed directly through the app. that's the kind of direction i think you should move toward.

and one more note about expression mode: it has the best sound design overall, but the sound it makes at 'idle' is this high-pitched whirr, and that noise alone keeps me from using it regularly. if that whirr weren't there, expression mode might actually become my default setting.

in-car & app customization - personal mode should really be a blend of the best parts of all the different driving modes. i want personal mode to truly mean personal. for example, i love the sounds from expression mode, but i don't want the rest of expression mode active; so why can't i pull just those sounds into personal, or bring any single setting from the other modes into personal mode? on the app side, my 2022 hyundai tucson actually offers more customization, especially around the climate controls. i get that you're aiming for a simple "one button, no thinking" climate concept, but i want the ability to build my own climate profiles: like a winter@80deg setting with seat heaters, or a summer@65 setting with the seat coolers on. the last-used climate setup isn't always what i want the car to return to when i get back in. tesla is really doing great things in their app right now; pretty much any function on the car has an api call and can be accessed directly through the app. that's the kind of direction i think you should move toward.

and one more note about expression mode: it has the best sound design overall, but the sound it makes at 'idle' is this high-pitched whirr, and that noise alone keeps me from using it regularly. if that whirr weren't there, expression mode might actually become my default setting.

from a mechanical standpoint the car is excellent, in line with what i've come to expect from my previous seven bmws. it drives smooth, is very quiet and feels luxurious.
all of the problems i've run into are tied to the software.

route planning -
there is room to improve the in-car navigation system.
1-you are unable to plan a charging route starting from anywhere other than where the vehicle is currently parked, and you cannot set a starting charge level different from the present state of charge. that makes it impossible to pre-plan the second leg of a longer trip. this information should be something you can input.
2-the route suggestions are nowhere near optimized. for instance, i recently drove from fairview to bayport. the nav gave me a plan with charging stops showing an eleven and a half hour trip. having made that drive before (though not in an ev), i knew there was a more direct way. by simply dragging the route magnet through a different city, the recalculated route ended up about an hour shorter. why should i have to fix that manually?
3-the mybmw app ought to provide ev-specific route planning, similar to what my wife gets with her mercedes app for her ev.
4-route planning on bmwusa.com is basically useless. try it. choose range and route, i7 e50 20", put in a starting point like 210 harbor view rd, seaview beach fl and a destination like lakeside toyota of fairview. the result is just a line on the map with state names. no city labels. no identified charging stops. nothing that actually helps an ev driver. on a previous attempt it also showed a "?" button that, when pressed, only told me i would need to charge somewhere on the way. that is not helpful.
5-i ended up having to build a spreadsheet and use my own numbers to plan the journey. i've asked the local "genius" for guidance, but the way bmw's supporting software is designed is beyond what she can assist with.
6-i'm still hoping the mistakes are mine and that you can show me a better way to use these tools. but as i see things right now, the limitations of bmw's route planing tools aren't just unhelpful - they feel insulting. maybe that would be borderline acceptable in an economy car, but not in the i7.

seat positioning -
most of the time, after i unlock, get in, start the car and buckle up, the driver's seat moves correctly from the comfort access spot to the stored position 1 for driving. however, roughly 20% of the time it doesn't move at all. and once it even slid further back instead. usually tapping the "1" button will fix it, but sometimes that button has to be held down, and sometimes only the seat controls on the door will get it to move. i suspect there might be some link to how and when i clear the nuisance disclaimer message.

updates -
not long ago i was away for about a week. the first time i drove the car after coming back, i found a lot of things had been reset. my seat memories had vanished. the custom wake word i'd set was no longer active. saying "hey bmw" did nothing, even though those options still showed as selected in the menus. there were also new displays in the instrument cluster when driving with assist plus.
it would help if:
1 - existing user settings were kept intact when an update is installed.
2-a simple message popped up at startup letting the driver know the vehicle might behave differently than it did on the last drive.

thank you for looking at my comments on this car. it's unfortunate that these frustrations exist. out of all the bmws i've owned, this is the one i am most eager to drive.

i would really like to get a response to the issues i've mentioned.

customer_feedback_verbatim: the auto time zone adjustment just does not function. the radio also fails to quiet when i give carplay voice commands. with a 291 mile range, the actual distance i can use is heavily cut because i only charge between 20% and 80%. right now the public charging network feels both unreliable and not sufficiently available. every leg of a trip easily ends up with an extra hour added for each charging stop. i still dont know for sure, but if the battery life really proves to be just 8 years then this purchase will have been a poor investment. my insurance premium has shot up by about 200% even though the car has all this safety equipment. the explanation given is that repairing that safety tech after a crash costs a lot more, and the insurers claim there is not enough data yet to justify lowering the rates. sun glare or heavy rain seem to mess with the cameras trying to read the surroundings, and then the system basically chooses to shut itself off because it sees too much risk. when i drive on a road running parallel to train tracks, and a side street that crosses those tracks comes up, the railroad crossing lights aimed at the train get misread by the car as a stop light intended for my parallel road. there is also one set of traffic signals that the car reads as if they were a yield sign. the navigation does not let me set a preference for electrify america chargers when the planned distance exceeds the current charge; it just picks the first charger it finds. for at least the first 3 years, that electrify america selection option really should be there.

customer_feedback_verbatim:
Customer stated that from the time he took delivery, roughly 70% of the times he starts the vehicle the eSIM icon in the iDrive menu bar shows that the Personal eSIM is not configured and not working. Customer stated that when this occurs he cannot stream anything to the Theater Screen in the rear. Customer stated that in these instances, the iDrive Tel > Mobile devices list has the Personal eSIM entry highlighted with the note "Setting up personal eSIM" beneath it, and it never progresses or finishes. Customer stated he has gone to the dealership Genius multiple times and that the Genius adjusts something in the myBMW app to get it working again. Customer stated the fix does not last and the eSIM soon goes back to not functioning. Customer stated that he has been able to connect the eSIM and stream to the Theater Screen on some occasions, but that most of the time it fails because the eSIM never fully completes setup and connection.

Writer checked AIR and confirmed vehicle integration level G070-23-03-553 is newer than the -540 level specified for AT&T Personal eSIM. Writer connected via RVG and verified the issue: the sim card symbol with an exclamation mark in the menu bar indicated an eSIM fault. Writer confirmed the customer's description that the Tel > Mobile devices screen shows Personal eSIM highlighted with "Setting up personal eSIM" that does not change. Writer confirmed the customer was signed into his BMW ID / driver profile. Customer verified in the myBMW app that the Personal eSIM was activated on AT&T and stated he has an unlimited plan for the eSIM. Writer verified the customer's iPhone 14 is on iOS 16.5.1 and that the myBMW app is current and operating correctly.

Writer guided the customer to iDrive Menu > Vehicle apps > System settings > Update apps and services. Customer selected Update apps and services, and iDrive reported the vehicle software is current. Writer then walked the customer through a 30-second iDrive reset. Writer had the customer use the myBMW app to deactivate the eSIM from the i7. Writer next directed the customer in iDrive to Menu > Apps > Personal Hotspot > Connect new device. When the QR code appeared on the Control Display, customer stated the dealership Genius had previously skipped this step and done something different in the myBMW app, though the customer could not remember the details. Writer instructed the customer to scan the QR code. Customer stated the QR code did not proceed to move his phone further through the setup flow.

Writer then advised the customer to re-activate the eSIM using the Personal eSIM section in the myBMW app. Customer entered his phone number but the process stopped, and the app indicated he needed to add service. Writer guided the customer to select the eSIM device in iDrive and choose Activate internet access. Customer followed this, and his phone was forwarded to the AT&T login page. Customer signed into his AT&T account and tried to re-activate the eSIM on the i7, then ended the RVG session. Customer reported that on the AT&T site he was being asked to add service and that he could not re-activate the eSIM this way.

Writer explained that the problem appeared to be related to the customer's AT&T account, since AT&T was requiring added service for eSIM activation. Writer recommended that the customer contact AT&T to confirm his account and eSIM plan are truly unlimited and compatible with the Personal eSIM. Customer insisted the fault was with BMW. Writer still advised the customer to perform a 70-second iDrive hard reset to restart the telematics unit, even though the symptoms pointed more toward an AT&T account issue than telematics. Writer also recommended the customer return to the dealership so the Genius could repeat the same method they had used before to start the eSIM without involving the QR code or AT&T portal. Writer encouraged the customer to ask the dealership service department to check for any possible hardware defects due to the repeated nature of the problem. Customer did not specify what he intended to do next. Writer advised that the customer could reach out again with further questions or updates, but that the immediate next steps lay with AT&T or the dealership. Customer acknowledged.

aspect_en: Drive control, Chassis dynamics, Occupant protection
customer_feedback_verbatim:
the car itself is quite nice, but there are a few areas that need improvement:

1-interior:
a-warm air isn't really warm enough and takes too long to build up. i have to put the temperature on max just to feel actual warmth.
b-the seats have plenty of adjustment options, but overall they are not very comfortable. maybe that's partly personal, but there should still be a default seat comfort you can expect at this level.
c-a rear-seat display should be standard at this price, not an extra-cost upgrade, especially nowadays when an oled screen is around 200$ for a consumer. if the motorization around it makes it pricey, that part should be the added cost.
d-the glossy trim shows fingerprints far too easily, and since everything is touch sensitive it's difficult to wipe it clean without accidentally changing settings.

2-driving experience:
a-for a car of this size, the steering feels a bit too wide. rear wheel steering seems like something that should be default for a premium vehicle like this.
b-overall the car is too needy, constantly popping up notifications, which can be distracting. the red light warning is not well tuned, as it will alert me even on the highway when it spots the signal for the entrance lane on the right. that is very distracting and frankly a bug.
c-switching out of autopilot isn't smooth enough, and the car behaves a bit stubborn. sometimes it decides to change lane at a very bad moment. for instance, if the navigation says i need to take an exit in under a mile, it shouldn't try to move into the opposite lane just to go faster.
d-the autopilot braking is quite harsh. even when it clearly detects the car ahead slowing, it reduces speed too late, making the brakes feel very strong.
e-when reactivating autopilot on streets with a speed limit, it should honor the current street limit, not only the setting. if i mistakenly turn the tempomat back on in a 25 zone, the car shouldn't start heading for 65.

my i7 has been an absolutely fantastic car so far, and the way it drives has felt perfect to me. it is extremely comfortable, and the overall quietness of the drivetrain and cabin is beyond what i have experienced with similar cars i owned before. the tech and amenities in the i7 meet or even surpass what i expect in this class. everyone who has ridden with me has been impressed with these same things. the range does drop in the winter, but for my daily use i find the range acceptable.

my only real issue with this particular car is that it arrived with bubbles in the sunroof glass, and the dealer is currently working on it. the car has been diagnosed with a manufacturer defect in the sunroof, with several small bubbles trapped between the glass layers of the panel. i am worried these imperfections could weaken the sunroof and affect safety over time, especially with temperature changes or impacts from rough or uneven roads. the team at bmw of Fairview has been great throughout all of this, showing professionalism, being transparent, and keeping me thoroughly informed while they resolve it. the problem, however, means the car needs a major teardown and repair, including removing the interior headliner, the pillar trim, the sun shade cassette, the windshield, and the driver assistance camera assembly, etc. since i have only had the car a few months, it is extremely frustrating to deal with such a big problem so early in ownership. i have barely had time to really enjoy what was supposed to be a flagship, brand-new vehicle before finding out it has to be significantly dismantled to fix this. as a long-time bmw fan and repeat owner, i have always respected the brand for its quality, precision, and innovation.

to date, the i7 has genuinely been a joy to own. in every other way it has met and even exceeded what i expect from a flagship executive sedan. the level of craftsmanship, the outstanding comfort, and the excellent noise isolation make each trip calm and very refined, which is exactly what i associate with bmw and the idea of the "ultimate driving machine." that makes this problem even more disheartening, since i expected years of worry-free enjoyment and trust in the car. with such a quiet cabin and electric drivetrain, i now fear that an invasive repair like this might never bring the car fully back to its original, factory-perfect state, and could introduce new shakes or rattles later.

customer_feedback_verbatim:
i have a 750e 2026, and this is my second 7 series model. from the very first day, the car has been making a repeating knocking sound from the right rear passenger side, very much like the automatic door lock noise (da-da). the dealership has been supportive, understanding, and professional while trying to track it down, and they have traced it to a valve that is supposed to push gas vapors toward the engine when a certain buildup level is reached.
this sound is distracting and extremely annoying to everyone in the car, and it happens while driving, when stopped, with a full tank, with a half tank, and so on. to me, that points to poor quality control on the manufacturer side, which is very disappointing. i highly doubt this is just a single isolated case and assume you have already heard about it. the 750e is marketed as your flagship, but with this issue it does not really feel like one, and i think it needs to be handled properly at the manufacturer level. i am also worried it could be a safety-related problem.
as a separate irritation, i would expect bmw to include safety features that even cheaper cars already have. specifically, there should be an optional audible alert for blind spot lane changes, in addition to the triangle symbol on the side mirrors. that triangle is hard to see, and a tone to warn that there is a vehicle in the lane would be very useful and much appreciated. make it an option that can be turned on or off, but at least offer it.
thank you for letting me share my disappointment; bmw management really should look into these matters. this is my third bmw, and i am starting to lose that pride in owning one. none of this is a criticism of my local dealership, they are always professional and supportive. honestly, without their effort to keep clients satisfied, i would most likely already be back in a mercedes. the dealer team truly acts like quintessential professionals and treats customers like family.
again, thanks for your time. you can reach out to me directly if you wish; coastal bmw - clearwater, fl has my contact information.
- david lane

this sound is distracting and extremely annoying to everyone in the car, and it happens while driving, when stopped, with a full tank, with a half tank, and so on. to me, that points to poor quality control on the manufacturer side, which is very disappointing. i highly doubt this is just a single isolated case and assume you have already heard about it. the 750e is marketed as your flagship, but with this issue it does not really feel like one, and i think it needs to be handled properly at the manufacturer level. i am also worried it could be a safety-related problem.
as a separate irritation, i would expect bmw to include safety features that even cheaper cars already have. specifically, there should be an optional audible alert for blind spot lane changes, in addition to the triangle symbol on the side mirrors. that triangle is hard to see, and a tone to warn that there is a vehicle in the lane would be very useful and much appreciated. make it an option that can be turned on or off, but at least offer it.
thank you for letting me share my disappointment; bmw management really should look into these matters. this is my third bmw, and i am starting to lose that pride in owning one. none of this is a criticism of my local dealership, they are always professional and supportive. honestly, without their effort to keep clients satisfied, i would most likely already be back in a mercedes. the dealer team truly acts like quintessential professionals and treats customers like family.
again, thanks for your time. you can reach out to me directly if you wish; coastal bmw - clearwater, fl has my contact information.
- david lane

aspect_en: Charging experience, Range management, V2X/Power supply
customer_feedback_verbatim: right now there is basically no charging network in places that feel safe. the car itself was pretty loud and it came across like the build quality was worse than the m8 we owned before, with a lot of road noise, mainly on the driver side. the vehicle is gorgeous and rides nicely, but i really think bmw should include adapters so you can charge at brighter, well lit stations. most of the chargers we found were out in the middle of nowhere, and many of them were not on charge america, so the 30 minutes of free charging perk almost never got used. i really liked the exterior styling and the interior design. i ended up giving it a rating of 3 because it seems fine for driving around town, but feels unsafe for long trips. my wife was nearly stuck in the middle of oklahoma because the charging station was closed and located inside a dealership. she had to sit charging for hours in a rough part of town, in an area with bad lighting. on top of all that, the safety system in the car and the steering assist stopped working early in the journey. overall, i honestly would not suggest buying an electric car right now, at least until bmw sorts out being able to charge safely while traveling.

customer_feedback_verbatim:
so far the car has been performing amazingly. it is very quiet, rides smooth, and is extremely comfortable. the auto drive / cruise control setup is good, but a bit confusing to switch between at first. i really wish there was clearer instruction and more direct control over the driving safety features. that stupid safety thing tries to brake constantly. and even when it needs to brake, why so hard and so early instead of more gradual? it makes me feel like i am driving badly and either irritating people by creeping toward stopped traffic or risking a wreak.

the touchscreens look great, but i would rather have more real buttons. it is awkward to tap the media "button" on the center console twice, you have to lift your finger fully and press again, which would be much simpler with a clicking button. all those controls could have been discrete buttons. there is no mute button on the steering wheel, which seems like a big oversight. and even when you do manage to hit the mute on the center armrest, it really just acts as pause - you can unmute but the player stays paused (at least on android with mediamonkey). i also don't get why the music doesn't actually pause when navigation gives directions; it just dips the volume like a radio, but a player could pause. my mercedes does both, with a steering wheel mute and pausing for instructions.

i also don't understand why the running lights stay on for hours; it seems tied to turning the car off then opening the door, or opening the door when the car goes to standby, but it's very confusing. the ac vents are useless if the car has been sitting in full sun, totally inadequate. i want finer control over a/c fan speed and vent routing - it's too easy for everything to get unsynced or for a small change to kick it out of auto mode. i wish the seat coolers were quieter. and i really wish there was an option without the glass roof, because that thing does nothing to block the sun and heat.

we absolutely love our i7. it rides so smoothly, looks really elegant, is packed with cool technology, and the real world range is quite good. we use it both for business and personal needs. we shuttle clients, mostly physicians at a clinic, and they are very impressed with the car and really like that it is an ev.

my spouse and i enjoy taking it everywhere. we have put close to 4800 miles on it in about 3 months, and it hardly feels like that much. it is a joy to drive on longer road trips.

there are a couple of things i would change. the subwoofer seems like it should be placed somewhere in the cabin. i think there is an upgraded diamond surround system that might add this. i owned a 2016 m5 before, and the bass in that car was just right. a friend has a 2024 ix, and i was amazed by the sound system in his.

ours is carbon black, so it gets washed often. one thing i noticed is that the rear trunk lid, especially the area under the rear bmw badge, traps a lot of water and it drains slowly. when it finally drains, it runs down onto the rear bumper and leaves water spots. we even use a blow dryer and it still causes some hassle. every car has its quirks, so i am not overly concerned.

also, i feel like the master window controls on the driver door should be moved back about 1-2 inches. even after 3 months, i still end up opening the rear windows when i mean to open the fronts. the placement feels unnatural. i'm 6 feet tall and have never really run into this in another vehicle.

overall, i really love this car and already look forward to owning another one someday. thanks for making such a gem of a vehicle.
